title: FiLM versus Mirror feature conditioning
hypothesis: For context-conditioned digit classification under four fixed input domains, a four-angle Givens feature View can improve quality over shared unconditioned features with a smaller actual inference payload than FiLM, while matching or exceeding same-dimensional grouped FiLM and rank-1 controls.
physical_object: One 64-64-10 MLP shared by four fixed pixel-permutation contexts.
mirror_coordinate: Four context-specific Givens angles over the first eight hidden activation coordinates before the classifier.
logical_multiplicity: Four context-conditioned digit classifiers from one shared MLP.

dataset.name: sklearn digits
dataset.contexts: four deterministic pixel-index permutations; labels unchanged
dataset.split: stratified 60/20/20 by base example; same identities across contexts; per-world seed

development.selection: minimum validation NLL averaged across four contexts and methods
development.allowed_tuning: select only shared/independent training LR from frozen grid

storage.authority: actual torch.save complete inference bank bytes after reload

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror improves mean accuracy over no-code shared baseline by >=1pp, within 2pp of independent, complete payload <=60% independent, and vs same-dimensional scale FiLM either >=1pp accuracy gain at byte-near cost or >=10% byte savings at <=0.5pp loss.
failure_gate: Quality/storage gate fails in >=2 fresh worlds or grouped FiLM/rank-1 matches or dominates at equal/lower complete bytes and active compute.
boundaries: digits context classification only, not a Transformer feature-conditioning benchmark
fixed updates are not capacity evidence
